# OTP Bank & GrowthBook: PoC discussion
Date: 2026-10-26 | Duration: 61.27000045776367m

## Summary
The discussion covered how namespaces can isolate experiment audiences and how API workflows may be needed for launch gates, conflict warnings, alerts, and approvals because GrowthBook lacks some governance features natively. GrowthBook does not provide a complete interaction inventory, so a separate registry may remain necessary. BigQuery can support Firebase analysis using exposure events, variant and experiment identifiers, but Azure policies make BigQuery difficult and Oracle remains on-premise. Three architecture paths were identified: managed ClickHouse, self-hosted GrowthBook, or an Azure data lake, while CRM data mapping remains open. The POC should prioritize mobile and CRM, validate completed Firebase experiments, metrics, and fact tables, and support cross-team testing involving mobile, marketing automation, and potentially web. A 30-day POC with a possible 15-day extension was discussed, alongside a potential Q1 launch, free SDK initialization before the trial, and a Microsoft Teams channel pending ownership confirmation.

## Keywords
Experiment governance, Namespaces, Firebase validation, Azure data architecture, Marketing automation, PoC planning

# OTP Bank & GrowthBook: Commercial meeting
Date: 2026-11-25 | Duration: 14.800000190734863m

## Summary
GrowthBook integration is planned in stages, beginning with the mobile application this quarter, followed by marketing automation integration and a first experiment next quarter. The customer team is responsible for setting up the open-source platform, SDKs, and data connection, after which James will involve technical solutions resources. A formal POC may begin in January, with an enterprise license, support, training, onboarding, and implementation assistance available. Use cases and success criteria will be agreed before evaluating whether to proceed. The proposed self-hosted model includes a $150,000 annual platform license, unlimited experiments, no monthly active-user metering, and $1,000 per annual seat; a 30-seat example totals $180,000 annually. Seats apply across user roles and can be added in blocks of five, with mid-year additions prorated. A one-year agreement is the baseline, while a two-year term may receive a 5% license discount. GrowthBook will provide both self-hosted and cloud proposals for budgeting, including seat-based and experiment-based options.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Proof of concept, Self-hosting, Enterprise licensing, Experimentation, Marketing automation
